clue.text: Recognise the flower in bloom

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part, the pick of the bunch
a flower in bloom is out

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a plant in full flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The flower' is not a plant but the best of a group, as in 'the flower of youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out or identify something is to recognise it.

clue.text: Effort abandoned to obtain leave

parts.note: a push is a determined effort
a match called off is abandoned

explanation.surface: A struggle is given up in order to get time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean depart, go away.

clue.text: Be persuasive and deliver a guilty verdict

explanation.surface: A jury is convincing and finds the defendant guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that convinces people is said to have force; read literally, the phrase is taking a guilty finding to a court.

clue.text: Notice in newspaper, appeal following outside broadcast

indicators.note: the appeal comes after the broadcast in the answer, so it is placed second

parts.note: it is sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A newspaper announcement follows a plea made in a live outside transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' here is the indefinable attraction called 'it', not a plea; 'following' places it after the broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A death announcement printed in a paper is a short form of obituary.

clue.text: Originally earn the capital abroad

indicators.note: done in an original way, so the letters of the following words are rearranged freshly

parts.note: used as written for the anagram
used as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone first earned money in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' rearranges EARN THE; this spelling is the older English form of the Iranian capital's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Iran, a foreign capital.

clue.text: Composer's note written in low key

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'composer is', so the definition is the composer

indicators.note: the note is set down inside the word for low

parts.note: feeling low is feeling down
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A musician's tune is scored in a minor, sombre key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written in' places the note inside the word for low. John Dowland was an English lutenist and songwriter around 1600.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowland was a Renaissance writer of lute songs.

clue.text: Scornful of French naval leader being in command

parts.note: de is the French for 'of'

indicators.note: the naval leader sits inside the word for command

parts.note: a fiat is an authoritative decree or command

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An admiral from France is contemptuous of those he commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French naval leader' looks like an admiral, but 'of French' and 'naval leader' are separate pieces, and 'being in' sets the leader inside a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone openly resisting or disdaining authority is defiant.

clue.text: Go and be successful

explanation.surface: Advice to set out and prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that goes is functioning; a plan that succeeds is said to come off.

clue.text: Like Australian, unsentimental, actually

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a prosaic, unemotional manner is matter-of-fact

explanation.surface: An Aussie described as blunt and down to earth, in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in fact, really.

clue.text: Dutch duke's gone off causing resentment

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: gone off means turned bad, so the letters of the word are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: used as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A Dutch nobleman's departure causes ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' reads as the duke leaving, but 'off' means spoilt and scrambles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to be in a state of indignant anger.

clue.text: Even more advanced and outspoken

parts.note: a straight line is even, level
forward means further ahead, more advanced

explanation.surface: Something is still further ahead and frank as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank, direct manner is one that speaks plainly.

clue.text: Gem's left out at most times

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is taken out of the word

parts.note: 'only' means no more than, at most
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: A jewel is usually omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' removes L from ONLY to leave ONY; the 's of 'Gem's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony used as a semiprecious stone.

clue.text: Quiet, retiring manner shown by male monarch

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for manner is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A king displays a shy, reserved demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns AIR into RIA. Priam was king of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy during the Trojan War.

clue.text: Relax in an area set aside

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Unwind in a space reserved for that purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across arEA SEt; 'aside' completes the surface picture of a reserved space.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen tension or effort is to relax.

clue.text: Girl takes road into cathedral city

indicators.note: the road is put inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a small city in Cambridgeshire with a famous cathedral
the M1 motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A young woman drives along a road into a city with a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its name is written MI here. Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Smooth union leader seen in bar

indicators.note: the leader appears inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar and save both mean except

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A slick trade union official is spotted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it means 'except', SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave manner is polished and urbane.

clue.text: Staff provide backing for base attendant

indicators.note: the staff stands behind the base, so it is placed after it

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
to staff is to man

explanation.surface: Employees support a domestic servant's foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun but is the verb MAN; 'provide backing for' puts it behind FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A liveried servant who waits on a household.

clue.text: Contracted out quarter agreed in SW town

indicators.note: out stands for outside, so the tightened word is placed round the quarter

parts.note: contracted muscles are tight, taut
N, north, is a compass quarter
'you're on' means agreed

explanation.surface: Work is outsourced to a district of a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is short for outside here. Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is Somerset's county town in the south-west of England.

clue.text: Maybe an automatic's 'not finished spin?

indicators.note: the word is left without its final letter

parts.note: a handgun of which an automatic is another kind; 'maybe' marks it as a loose example, and 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A gun owner wonders whether the pistol's mechanism has stopped turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not finished' drops the last R from REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn round on an axis is to rotate.

clue.text: Angry earful about cardinal's negative response

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the cardinal point
angry suggests disturbance, so the letters of earful are rearranged

parts.note: S, south, is a cardinal point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cardinal receives a furious telling-off for saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but gives S, a compass point; 'Angry' rearranges EARFUL round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining a request is saying no.

clue.text: Vulnerable divorcee worked as a model

parts.note: a former spouse is an ex
a model posed for the artist

explanation.surface: A former wife who sat for artists is now defenceless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unprotected and open to attack.

clue.text: Hide a number remaining in pocket

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
what remains is left over
someone in pocket is up, ahead financially

explanation.surface: Someone conceals a figure left in their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealment, to conceal something from view.

clue.text: Six-footer escorted by jazz fan to a musical piece

indicators.note: the insect is flanked by the jazz fan, who walks either side

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for an enthusiast
an ant is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: A very tall person is accompanied by a jazz lover to a concert work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six legs, flanked by the jazz fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral work with solo voices, usually in several movements.

clue.text: Claim related to being in force

indicators.note: the word for related to sits inside the word for force

parts.note: to press is to force
of means concerning, related to

explanation.surface: An assertion connected with a law in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or assert something openly.

clue.text: Note outstanding features

parts.note: F is a musical note
ace means excellent, outstanding

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a person's striking traits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's features together make up their visage.

clue.text: Points out clip in supporting structure

indicators.note: out stands for outside, so the points go round the clip

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are compass points
a pin is a clip or fastener

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a fastener in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is short for outside: the compass points wrap the fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone supports the body; a book's back also holds it together.

clue.text: In that case fellow in Iceland will get nothing

indicators.note: the fellow is put inside the country's code

parts.note: IS is the international vehicle code for Iceland
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man in Iceland is left with nothing, should that happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A conditional phrase meaning if that is true.

clue.text: Sounds like it's fine food

indicators.note: the word for fine is heard as another spelling

parts.note: fine weather is fair

explanation.surface: It seems this cooking is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' could mean a penalty; it is FAIR, said to sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The meals on offer, as in 'traditional country cooking'.

clue.text: Save article up for Middle Easterner

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: save and bar both mean except
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Rescue a newspaper item about a man from the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR + A read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Arabian peninsula or the Arab world.

clue.text: Clara praises its new architectural feature

indicators.note: the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: used as written for the anagram
used as written for the anagram
used as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Clara admires a building's novel design element.
explanation.definitionFit: A helical flight of steps winding round a central post.

clue.text: Trainee denies spilling oil

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate

indicators.note: spilling scatters the letters of denies

parts.note: used as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A learner denies knocking over the oil can.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on British cars; 'spilling' rearranges DENIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaxseed pressed for an oil used in paints and wood finish.

clue.text: Run into a bar on American building plant

indicators.note: the run is put inside the following words

parts.note: bar and but both mean except
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pub on an American building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub but means BUT, except. The plant is the strawberry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of evergreen shrubs including the strawberry tree.
